QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_15

question.text: When is an external member of the Investment Committee of a Cat III AIF NOT required to secure fresh consent from 75% of investors (by value) for their appointment?

answer.text: Whenever the AMC management unilaterally decides.
When the investor has a family relation with the proposed member.

When their name was already disclosed in the PPM or fund-document at the time of on-boarding investors; also for ex-officio members like Sponsor/Sponsor Group/Investment Manager Group changes in official capacity.

explanation.text: The Logic: External IC members whose names ARE disclosed in PPM/fund document at on-boarding do not need fresh 75% consent. Also, consent is not required for change in ex-officio external members (Sponsor, Sponsor Group, Investment Manager Group, or investors in their official capacity). The Trap: One distractor ignores investor rights; another overstates the threshold; another invents a family-tie exemption. Note: Page 277 of the workbook sets out both carve-outs: prior PPM disclosure at onboarding and ex-officio changes in official capacity. The 75% test is by value of investment, not by number of investors.
